claims.text: Low-temperature in-situ annealing at 250–300 °C selectively modifies the grain-boundary structure of FeMnNiGeSi-type nanoscale films and nanoribbons.
The specified annealing treatment relieves internal or residual stresses in the material.
Grain-boundary modification and stress relief modulate exchange interactions in the films.
Exchange interactions govern a first-order magnetostructural transition in these FeMnNiGeSi-type films and nanoribbons.
Annealing may initiate short-range ordering as a consequence of stress relief.
Annealing slightly increases the density of modified grain boundaries.
The annealing-induced microstructural evolution alters exchange interactions among nanoscale domains.
Altered exchange interactions adjust the kinetics of the first-order magnetic phase transition.
The annealed films will exhibit lower thermal hysteresis than the as-deposited baseline under applied fields below 0.5 T.
The annealed films will exhibit a shifted magnetocaloric-response peak relative to the as-deposited baseline.
The annealed films may exhibit a broadened magnetocaloric-response curve relative to the as-deposited baseline.
The annealed films will exhibit a lower magnetocaloric peak magnitude than the as-deposited baseline.
An inert atmosphere prevents oxidation during the annealing treatment.
Magnetic-cooling cycle rates must be matched to heat-transfer limitations.
Phase decomposition or significant diffusion would confound attribution of magnetic changes to grain-boundary modification and stress relief.
